content:
maria: Heads-up — during the staged rollout of the new safetensors sharding layout I've been seeing a thundering-herd style spike from clients doing simultaneous warmup handshakes. Prod traces show lots of repeated GET /weights/prefetch?shard=... calls when we reassign shards.

aj: Yep, saw that in the trace. Clients are retrying aggressively when they hit transient 503s during manifest switch. No jitter + high concurrency = storm.

devon: My quick thought: make the handshake two-step. Step 1) manifest pin check + quick metadata response. Step 2) client requests a warmup reservation token. Server can grant a limited number of concurrent warmups per-bundle. That should reduce thundering herd.

sam: Also worth noting that parsing safetensors headers currently blocks the network thread for ~30-50ms per small shard. If clients try to parse in-line it adds up. We should move header parsing off the hot path or return a tiny header-only response first so clients can decide.

leo: Could we expose a warmup lease header from the server like:
X-Warmup-Lease: ttl=30;max_prefetch=4;lease_id=abc123
Then client can back off when lease is absent or full.

maria: Proposed client-side changes (short-term): limit concurrent warmups per-model-per-process to 3, use exponential backoff with jitter for retries, and fall back to index-first fetch if warmup is denied. Example config snippet:```json
{
  "warmup": {
    "max_concurrent": 3,
    "initial_delay_ms": 100,
    "max_delay_ms": 8000,
    "jitter": 0.25,
    "fallback": "index-first"
  }
}
```
aj: That looks reasonable. Server-side we can return 429 or 503 with a Retry-After when lease is exceeded, and include the lease header when accepting. Clients interpret 429 as lease denied and back off.

devon: Edge-case: mixed-format bundles (safetensors + quantized .bin) — lease/granularity should be per-bundle id, not per-shard, otherwise clients will fight for same bundle. Also the lease should include a lease_id so retries can piggyback on the same lease.

sam: Short-term plan: server returns X-Warmup-Lease or 429; client implements concurrent limit + backoff + fallback. Long-term: central warmup coordinator service that tracks live warmups per-cluster and offers better scheduling and preemption.

deploybot: deploybot: canary deployed warmup-lease handler to staging (canary-5). Logs at /services/weights/warmup.

aj: Small but important: when a client gets lease denied, it should try a tiered fetch strategy: HEAD -> range-based chunk -> full fetch only if necessary. Avoid full shard pulls on denial.

maria: Action items: @sam to draft RFC follow-up with interface sketches and lease semantics; @aj to add client backoff + concurrent limit; @devon to add lease header support and per-bundle semantics on server; i'll run a load test against canary and post results here. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll start the RFC draft today and include perf numbers for header-only response vs full header parse.

maria: Thanks everyone — let's reconvene after the RFC draft.
